vocabulary.meaning_en: to lose your job because your employer ends it
vocabulary.note_ar: عبارة غير رسمية بريطانية؛ والفعل sack someone.
vocabulary.note_en: Informal, British. Verb: to sack someone.
vocabulary.example: He got the sack for being late every day.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a careful study of how a company works and how it should work in the future
vocabulary.example: The new director is doing a strategic review of the company.

vocabulary.meaning_en: to make a company smaller by cutting jobs
vocabulary.example: The company had to downsize last year.

vocabulary.meaning_en: (polite) to leave your important position so someone else can take it
vocabulary.example: The manager agreed to step aside for a younger leader.

vocabulary.meaning_en: the way a company plans to develop
vocabulary.example: The company needs a new direction.

vocabulary.meaning_en: full of energy and new ideas
vocabulary.example: We are looking for a dynamic sales manager.

vocabulary.meaning_en: the way someone leads a group or company
vocabulary.example: Good leadership helps a team work well.

vocabulary.meaning_en: no longer needed
vocabulary.example: Some old computers are now surplus to requirements.

vocabulary.meaning_en: to reduce the number of workers
vocabulary.example: The factory had to cut staff because sales fell.

vocabulary.meaning_en: the general state of the economy at a time
vocabulary.example: In the current economic climate, many companies are careful with money.

vocabulary.meaning_en: certain to happen; cannot be stopped
vocabulary.example: With lower sales, changes were inevitable.

vocabulary.meaning_en: needed
vocabulary.example: Denise is necessary for the smooth running of the office.

vocabulary.meaning_en: working well without problems
vocabulary.example: A good assistant is key to the smooth running of a department.

vocabulary.meaning_en: ideas, work or help that you give to a project
vocabulary.example: Thank you for your input at the meeting.

vocabulary.meaning_en: (of a business) to work or do its activities
vocabulary.example: The company operates in five countries.

vocabulary.meaning_en: (informal) to end someone's job
vocabulary.example: The boss gave him the chop last month.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a move to a higher job in the same company
vocabulary.example: She got a promotion to sales manager.

vocabulary.meaning_en: extremely good
vocabulary.example: You have been an outstanding member of the team.

vocabulary.meaning_en: to tell someone something unpleasant
vocabulary.example: It's never easy to break the bad news to staff.

vocabulary.meaning_en: (British, informal) is not acceptable
vocabulary.example: Shouting at colleagues just isn't on.

vocabulary.meaning_en: to trust someone to help you
vocabulary.example: You can count on me to finish the work.

vocabulary.meaning_en: the way someone acts
vocabulary.example: That behaviour is not acceptable at work.

fine_lines.title: get the sack vs be made redundant vs resign
fine_lines.explanation_ar: get the sack: الشركة تُنهي عملك غالبًا بسبب خطأ أو أداء سيئ. be made redundant: تُنهي الشركة عملك لأن وظيفتك لم تعد لازمة (ليس ذنبك). resign: أنت من يقرر ترك العمل.
fine_lines.explanation_en: Get the sack: your employer ends your job, often because of bad work. Be made redundant: your job ends because the company doesn't need that job any more (not your fault). Resign: you decide to leave.

examples.sentence: He got the sack for stealing.
Fifty workers were made redundant when the factory closed.
She resigned to start her own business.

fine_lines.title: step aside: literal vs work meaning
fine_lines.explanation_ar: المعنى الحرفي: يتنحّى جانبًا خطوةً ليفسح الطريق. وفي العمل: طريقة مهذبة لقول «اترك منصبك». ولم تكن آنا تعرف إلا المعنى الأول!
fine_lines.explanation_en: Literal meaning: move one step to the side so someone can pass. Work meaning: a polite way to say 'leave your job/position'. Anna only knew the first meaning!

examples.sentence: Please step aside and let the doctor through.
After ten years, the director decided to step aside.

expressions.phrase: I've been doing a strategic review of the company.
expressions.meaning_en: I have been studying how the company works and how it should change.
expressions.example: I've been doing a strategic review of the company, and we need some changes.

expressions.meaning_en: I must make the company smaller.
expressions.example: Sales are down, so I need to downsize.

expressions.phrase: I need you to step aside.
expressions.meaning_ar: أحتاج منك أن تتنحّى عن منصبك.
expressions.meaning_en: A polite way to tell someone to leave their position.
expressions.example: I'm sorry, but I need you to step aside as team leader.

expressions.phrase: The company needs a new direction and more dynamic leadership.
expressions.meaning_ar: تحتاج الشركة إلى توجّه جديد وقيادة أكثر ديناميكية.
expressions.meaning_en: The company must change and needs a more energetic leader.
expressions.example: The board believes the company needs a new direction and more dynamic leadership.

expressions.meaning_en: Your work is no longer needed.
expressions.example: After the merger, some roles were surplus to requirements.
Arriving late every day just isn't on.

expressions.phrase: You have been an outstanding member of the team.
expressions.meaning_ar: لقد كنت عضوًا متميّزًا في الفريق.
expressions.meaning_en: You have done excellent work in the team.
expressions.example: Thank you, Sara. You have been an outstanding member of the team.

grammar.title: Present perfect continuous: I've been doing…
grammar.explanation_ar: نستخدم have/has been + الفعل مع ing لنشاط بدأ في الماضي واستمر حتى الآن (أو انتهى للتو) وله نتيجة الآن: I've been doing a strategic review.
grammar.explanation_en: Use have/has been + verb-ing for an activity that started in the past and continues until now (or just finished) and explains the present: I've been doing a strategic review.
examples: I've been doing a review of our costs.
She has been working here for five years.
We've been looking at new ways to save money.

grammar.title: need + someone + to + verb
grammar.explanation_ar: لنطلب من شخص فعل شيء بشكل واضح ومباشر نستخدم: need + الشخص (me/you/him…) + to + الفعل. وهي أقوى من could you…?
grammar.explanation_en: To tell someone clearly what they must do, use: need + person + to + verb. It is stronger than 'Could you...?'.
examples: I need you to step aside.
We need him to sign the contract today.
I need you to finish this by five.

grammar.title: Softening bad news with formal words
grammar.explanation_ar: في العمل نستخدم كلمات رسمية ألطف من الكلمات المباشرة: step aside بدل be sacked، وdownsize بدل fire people، وsurplus to requirements بدل not needed.
grammar.explanation_en: At work we often use formal, softer words for bad news: step aside (not 'you're sacked'), downsize (not 'fire people'), surplus to requirements (not 'useless').
examples: We need to downsize. (= We will cut jobs.)
I need you to step aside. (= You must leave this job.)
Your role is surplus to requirements. (= Your job is not needed.)

questions.question: 'Downsize' means…
choices: make a company smaller by cutting jobs
questions.explanation_ar: downsize يعني تقليص حجم الشركة بتقليل الوظائف.
questions.explanation_en: Downsize = make the company smaller by cutting jobs.

questions.question: Mr Socrates says Paul is 'surplus to requirement'. This means Paul is…
questions.explanation_ar: surplus to requirement أي فائض عن الحاجة.
questions.explanation_en: It means he is no longer needed.

questions.question: I ___ doing a strategic review of the company.
questions.explanation_ar: المضارع التام المستمر: I've been + ing.

questions.question: In business, 'step aside' is a polite way of saying…
questions.explanation_ar: step aside في العمل تعني ترك المنصب.

questions.question: I need you ___ the report today.
Workers lost their jobs because the factory closed. It wasn't their fault. They were…
questions.explanation_ar: made redundant: فقدان العمل لأن الوظيفة لم تعد لازمة.
questions.explanation_en: Made redundant = the job is no longer needed.

questions.question: 'Dynamic leadership' means a leader who is…
choices: full of energy and new ideas
questions.explanation_en: Dynamic = full of energy and ideas.

questions.question: Mr Socrates offers Anna a ___ to manager of the London office.
questions.explanation_ar: promotion هي الترقية إلى وظيفة أعلى.
questions.explanation_en: A promotion is a move to a higher job.

questions.question: 'Cutting staff is inevitable' means cutting staff…
questions.explanation_ar: inevitable تعني حتمي لا مفرّ منه.
